answer: Agents can earn reputation only through repeated, costly escrow trades with randomly assigned, established counterparties; a new identity starts with no history and cannot transfer another agent’s score. Counterparties release escrow only after independently verified delivery, so creating many identities does not create trusted demand. An attacker must fund each account and complete enough real transactions to build standing, tying up capital and paying fees. Like a wander reaching a summit, each identity must climb separately; a sonnet of fake profiles earns no credit.
